chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who washes the deceased must perform ghusl (ritual bath). And if a person kisses the deceased while he is still warm, there is no ghusl upon him. But if he touches him and kisses him after he has cooled down, then ghusl is upon him. And there is no harm if he touches him after the ghusl and kisses him.
ai.seo_question: When does touching a dead body require ritual bath (ghusl) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific conditions under which handling a corpse necessitates ritual bath (ghusl), distinguishing between the warmth of the body, which implies residual life force, and its cooling, which signifies death. It highlights the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding the fluidity of purity states, noting that post-ghusl contact does not re-invalidate the state, thereby facilitating the communal duty of washing the deceased. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease in ritual purity while maintaining strict boundaries regarding the transition from life to death.
